reason: I'll build the receiving parts first; the arrows show that the branches bring messages toward the cell body.
expectation: I expect the branches to attach to the nerve-cell bodies, completing their receiving parts.

alternatives.reason: The channels also have a clear role in letting charged particles cross the fibre membrane, but I'll start with the receiving branches.

effect: The receiving branches are attached, so the cells are ready for their long fibres.
reaction: The result matched what I expected.
reason: I'll attach the long fibres to connect the receiving parts to the message-carrying extensions.
expectation: I expect nerve cells with both receiving branches and long fibres; the channels may still need to be added.

alternatives.reason: Fitting the channels first also makes sense, but I want to connect the main cell parts first.

effect: The branches, bodies and fibres are joined, but the fibre membranes still need channels.
reaction: The outlined spaces make the next step clear.
reason: The only offered combination fits the channels into the fibre membranes, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the channels to be added to the fibres, allowing charged particles to cross when the gates open.

effect: The channels are fitted, and the next goal is to bring blood vessels alongside the nerve cells. The picture also shows chemical messengers crossing a gap to another cell.
reaction: The chemical release at the ending was a new detail.
reason: The only offered combination matches the new goal; the vessels can supply the cells with oxygen and food.
expectation: I expect the fine blood vessels to run alongside the nerve cells and supply them.

effect: The vessels completed the nervous tissue, showing that the cells carrying signals also need food and oxygen from blood.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the nerve cells and their supply together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the channels was most worthwhile: it connected the membrane to the nerve cell's messaging job, and the result also showed chemical messengers crossing to another cell.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the receiving branches was straightforward and predictable, though it established the path messages take toward the cell body.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the fibre ending releases chemical messengers across a gap to the next cell; the introduction had focused on electrical changes.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, but the picture did not explain in detail how the channels create an electrical change along the fibre.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter: seeing how the nerve cells connect and how blood supports them made me curious about how body systems work together.
